question: What durable write-authorization contract should persistent MCP policies use across upgrades?
rationale: The current patch both treats stored config as write consent and resolves broad selectors against an evolving registry, so maintainers must decide whether future matching writes are authorized automatically.

options.title: Require exact persistent writes
options.body: Allow broad read selectors but require exact tool names for every persistently authorized write capability.

options.title: Accept dynamic selector expansion
options.body: Document that service, risk, and wildcard selectors intentionally authorize present and future matching write tools within baked safety ceilings.

options.title: Keep runtime write consent
options.body: Use stored config only as a non-widenable selector ceiling and continue requiring --allow-write for every write-enabled process.

recommendation.title: Require exact persistent writes
recommendation.body: Allow broad read selectors but require exact tool names for every persistently authorized write capability.

likelyOwner.reason: The current MCP/config history and authorship make this the clearest available owner for the permanent authorization contract.
